newsitem.title: UK: Dominion has 50 percent E.Midland acceptances.
newsitem.headline: Dominion has 50 percent E.Midland acceptances.

text.p: Dominion Resources said Thursday stockholders have tendered or agreed to tender 50.3 percent of the outstanding shares of East Midlands Electricity in response to its $2.15 billion takeover bid for the British regional electric company.
Dominion said it had already purchased about 15 percent of the shares at 670 pence ($11.16) each.

The British government on Wednesday said it would not refer the bid to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission. Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang said that Dominion had given assurances to address regulatory concerns.
Dominion's offer is open until Jan. 10.
It said that the 15 percent stake had been purchased on its behalf by DR Investments, a wholly owned subsidiary of Dominion, which is based in Richmond, Va.
East Midlands shares closed 3-1/2 pence firmer at 665 ($11.08). Dominion shares were unchanged at $38.125 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
